I have this really cool smart watch with a lot of interactive capabilities.

It reacts to voice, so I can just ask what time it is, and it will tell me.

Same goes for the weather or directions for example. It's really convenient.

Aside from that it has some neat social features as well.

You can change it's looks, so you'll have a different one whenever you want to, keeping things interesting.

It doesn't cost a boatload of your hard earned money, and there's no proprietary chargers or anything, which is an added benefit.

I don't have a smart one. IMO the battery of a watch should last at least a year. And a watch has one single purpose, display time.

In the same vein, a phone has a single purpose to call, but it has expanded to take over other functions making it much more useful.

But I agree that a one-day battery life is pretty poor and it holds me back from getting a smartwatch.

I've got a Pebble. I use it daily and chose it because it was the first of the modern generation and I still use it because it's still the best (will try Pebble Time next month when that arrives).

I use it daily as my running coach, and it displays the information that I want when I want: time and temp always (no arm waving to get it to wake up) and it does text, caller id, and email summaries when relevant (that's great when I'm in a meeting, on my motorcycle, or other situations when I can't go for my phone. And I only think about charging it once a week.

I haven't checked pricing on other phones, but I think Pebble is still like half the price of other smart watches.

It just displays the sender and first ...I dunno maybe 256 characters. It's enough that I can decide if it is important enough to stop what I'm doing and get my phone or computer out.

I did talk to a friend about a watch that had its own SIM card and could take calls directly, which sounds cool, but isn't something I think I would need.

I can't imagine the watch ever being a primary device, but I've benefitted from a secondary device and it's continuous but unobtrusive presence.
